screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows an AC source connected to one electromagnetic component — a resistor, inductor, or capacitor — and its voltage and current phasors.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has controls for the component type, its value, the source voltage and frequency, playback, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a component and explore how its phasor relates to the AC drive.

currentDetails.resistor: A resistor is connected. Its current is in phase with the source voltage.
currentDetails.inductor: An inductor is connected. Its current lags the source voltage by 90 degrees.
currentDetails.capacitor: A capacitor is connected. Its current leads the source voltage by 90 degrees.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a series RLC circuit driven by an AC source, with resistor, inductor, and capacitor voltage phasors closing back onto the source phasor.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has controls for R, L, and C, the source voltage and frequency, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Adjust R, L, and C to see how the series impedance and voltage triangle change.

currentDetails.inductive: The circuit is inductive: the source voltage leads the current, so the net reactance points up.
currentDetails.capacitive: The circuit is capacitive: the source voltage lags the current, so the net reactance points down.
currentDetails.resonant: The circuit is at resonance: the inductive and capacitive voltages cancel and the current is in phase with the source voltage.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the series RLC circuit swept across driving frequency, with the phase triangle alongside impedance-versus-frequency and current-versus-frequency curves.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Sweep the driving frequency to find resonance, where the reactances cancel and the phase angle goes to zero.

resonance.currentDetails: The Resonance screen is in its initial state.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the instantaneous power over a cycle, with the average real power and the oscillating reactive component shaded separately and a power-factor readout.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Adjust the load to see how the power factor changes and how a reactive load delivers zero net energy.

power.currentDetails: The Power screen is in its initial state.
